name: Geraniol

pubchem.title: Geraniol
pubchem.description: Geraniol is a monoterpenoid consisting of two prenyl units linked head-to-tail and functionalised with a hydroxy group at its tail end. It has a role as a volatile oil component, a fragrance, an allergen and a plant metabolite. It is a primary alcohol, a 3,7-dimethylocta-2,6-dien-1-ol and a monoterpenoid.

evidence: Measured in 3 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.06–0.14% of total volatiles (0.012–0.028mg per chew).

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Geraniol is a monoterpenoid, a type of volatile aromatic molecule that gives many flowers and herbs their signature sweet, rosy scent. As a primary alcohol built from two linked prenyl units, it is widely used as a fragrance in perfumes and cosmetics. You encounter it daily in the aroma of fresh roses, the zest of citrus fruits, and the complex bouquet of certain wines and teas.
consumer_summary.found_in: It is famously abundant in roses and geraniums, but it also flavors everyday foods and drinks. You can find geraniol in lemongrass, lemons, ginger, grapes, and even the hops used to brew beer.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to geraniol because of its broad biological activity, particularly its potential to manage oxidative stress and inflammation. With over 2,600 published papers, scientists are exploring how this fragrant molecule interacts with cellular pathways, including its effects on bacterial growth and metabolic health. The strongest evidence so far comes from human observational studies (Oxford level 2b). If these properties hold up in clinical trials, geraniol could become a valuable tool for developing new protective therapies and high-value biochemicals.

structure_function.statement: Geraniol may support the body's natural defenses against oxidative stress.
structure_function.basis: This rests on 33 papers, including 5 human observational studies and 22 animal studies.

structure_function.statement: Early work points toward geraniol having properties that may support microbial balance.
structure_function.basis: This is based on 27 papers, including human observational research and in vitro microbial sensitivity tests.

structure_function.statement: Geraniol is being studied for its potential to support healthy inflammatory responses.
structure_function.basis: This rests on 24 papers, primarily human observational and animal research.

structure_function.statement: Geraniol may act as a natural deterrent against insects.
structure_function.basis: This is supported by 9 papers, including human observational and animal studies.

structure_function.statement: Early work points toward geraniol supporting cellular health in the nervous system.
structure_function.basis: This rests on 7 papers, including human observational and animal research.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether geraniol can influence cellular apoptosis and tumor growth pathways, which could eventually inform new supportive oncology treatments.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial in humans to evaluate the efficacy and safety of geraniol supplementation alongside standard care, measuring tumor markers and progression-free survival over 12 months.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Early animal work points toward geraniol interacting with pain signaling pathways, raising the question of whether it could serve as a natural analgesic.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A Phase I/II human clinical trial administering a standardized oral geraniol extract to healthy volunteers subjected to a controlled pain stimulus, measuring subjective pain scores and inflammatory biomarkers over a 24-hour period.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Scientists are investigating whether the calming aroma and systemic effects of geraniol can modulate the central nervous system to improve sleep quality.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, placebo-controlled human crossover trial testing nightly inhaled or oral geraniol over four weeks, using polysomnography to measure sleep latency, REM cycles, and total sleep time.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether geraniol can support gut health and manage age-related malnutrition by influencing digestive metabolism.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized controlled trial in older adults experiencing malnutrition, providing a daily geraniol-fortified food product for 12 weeks and measuring changes in body mass index, nutrient absorption markers, and gut microbiome composition.

consumer_summary.cautions: In industrial or highly concentrated forms, geraniol is recorded as an occupational exposure hazard and a known fragrance allergen, though dietary amounts found in food are generally recognized as safe.
consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: Best evidence so far is human observational work (Oxford 2b); most of the rest is animal and lab research.
